summary:
[  edit  ]
The LFO  CHOP  (low frequency oscillator) generates waves in real-time in two ways. It synthesizes curves using a choice of common waveforms like Sine or  Pulse , or it repeats a prepared incoming curve.
It steps through the waveform at a rate that depends on the Frequency parameter and the Octave Control input. To watch its behavior, attach a Trail  CHOP  to its output and alter the Frequency parameter.
Up to three input CHOPs can be connected to the LFO  CHOP :
Octave Control  - Without this first (optional) input, the frequency is simply the Frequency parameter. If this input is connected, every unit doubles the frequency: When Octave Control is 1, the frequency is double, when it is 2 it is 4x, when it is -1 the frequency is half the Frequency parameter and when it is 0, there is no change in the frequency.
Reset  - The seond (optional) input contains on-off (<=0 or >0) that restarts the channels of the oscillator from the beginning of the wave. The reset depends on the setting of the Reset Condition menu. By default, when the Reset input goes from off to on, it resets the wave and starts the waveform immediately. If Reset Condition is set to "While On", the reset value will be held until the Reset input goes off. Reset means "stop the oscillator and cue it at the start of the waveform".
Source Wave  - The third (optional) input is a replacement of the waveform Type. It is a multi-sample  CHOP  curve and can contain any number of channels, limited to the channels defined on the Channel page. The waveform Type parameter is disabled.
The LFO  CHOP  can serve as a general motion time-warper and repeater. If you alter the Frequency, you can control the time warp.
Unlike the  Wave CHOP , this is a time-sliced  CHOP , that is, it generates its waveform as it goes, and speeds/slows how it steps through the waveform Type while the Frequency changes.  Unlike the  Audio Oscillator CHOP , the LFO  CHOP  is designed for non-audio frequencies.
See also:  Audio Oscillator CHOP ,  Wave CHOP ,  Pulse CHOP .

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: wavetype
parameters.description: ⊞  - The shape of the waveform to repeat, unless overridden by the Source Wave:

parameters.label: Sine
parameters.name: sin
parameters.description: (-1 to 1) A Sine wave.

parameters.label: Gaussian
parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: (0 to 1) A Gaussian (also known as a bell or normal) curve.

parameters.label: Triangle
parameters.name: tri
parameters.description: (-1 to 1) A ramp-up to 1 and ramp-down to -1 that can be shaped with the Bias parameter.

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.name: ramp
parameters.description: (0 to 1) A ramp from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Square
parameters.name: square
parameters.description: (-1 to 1) Step-up/step-down, with Bias control to make it rectangular.

parameters.label: Pulse
parameters.name: pulse
parameters.description: Produces a 1 for one sample, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: The LFO oscillates when 1, and stops when 0. Think of it like play and pause.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: The cycles per second of the oscillation. When the Octave Control input is connected, it alters the frequency exponentially.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Values output from the  CHOP  can have an offset added to them.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.name: amp
parameters.description: Values output from the  CHOP  can be scaled.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: Shape control for Triangle, Gaussian and Square waves. For triangle waves, it moves the peak. For square waves, it alters the width of the peak. Zero means no bias.

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.name: phase
parameters.description: A value of .5 is a phase shift of 180 degrees, or one half cycle.

parameters.label: Reset Condition
parameters.name: resetcondition
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu determines how the Reset input triggers resetting the channel(s).

parameters.label: Off to On
parameters.name: offtoon
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off to on.

parameters.label: While On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns off.

parameters.label: On to Off
parameters.name: ontooff
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on to off.

parameters.label: While Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns on.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: This toggle resets the channel(s) to 0 while On.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: This button instantly resets the channel(s) to 0.

parameters.label: Channel Name
parameters.name: channelname
parameters.description: A list of the names of the channels. You can put patterns like  chan[1-10]  to generate 10 channels. See  Pattern Expansion .

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: The sample rate of the  CHOP . The default sample rate is 60 samples per second.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
